title: Self-EvolveRec: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems with LLM-based Directional Feedback
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Feedback combining qualitative simulated-user critiques with quantitative diagnostics guides model evolution, and the diagnostics co-evolve with the model.
layout: 2 main panels, left-to-right; (a) split into two sub-panels, (b) a feedback loop
description: A wide figure in two parts. Part (a), Directional Feedback Generation, has two sub-panels separated by a vertical bar. (a.1) User Simulator: a stack of blue cards for a sampled user (persona, interaction history, recommendation list) feeds an orange User Simulator card. That card evaluates each recommended item and writes a qualitative feedback report. A green Summarized Feedback card follows, with failure phrases in red. (a.2) Diagnosis Tool: an orange card shows diagnostic analysis, with code icons, an embedding scatter plot and a histogram of ranking margin. Below them is structured diagnosis feedback with more red text. Part (b), Diagnosis Tool–Model Co-Evolution, is on the right. It shows the evolved codebase, the old diagnosis tool, a circled plus node, and the new diagnosis tool. Gray and green boxes for analysis and feedback connect to these with arrows. Pastel colors mark each module, and red highlights the key failures.
caption: Two core mechanism of Self-EvolveRec. (a) is the overview of the Directional Feedback Generation: (a.1) is the user simulator, (a.2) is the model diagnosis tool. (b) is the Diagnosis Tool - Model Co-evolution.
abstract: Traditional methods for automating recommender system design, such as Neural Architecture Search (NAS), are often constrained by a fixed search space defined by human priors, limiting innovation to pre-defined operators. While recent LLM-driven code evolution frameworks shift fixed search space target to open-ended program spaces, they primarily rely on scalar metrics (e.g., NDCG, Hit Ratio) that fail to provide qualitative insights into model failures or directional guidance for improvement. To address this, we propose Self-EvolveRec, a novel framework that establishes a directional feedback loop by integrating a User Simulator for qualitative critiques and a Model Diagnosis Tool for quantitative internal verification. Furthermore, we introduce a Diagnosis Tool - Model Co-Evolution strategy to ensure that evaluation criteria dynamically adapt as the recommendation architecture evolves. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Self-EvolveRec significantly outperforms state-of-the-art NAS and LLM-driven code evolution baselines in both recommendation performance and user satisfaction. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sein-Kim/self_evolverec.
